source_text: Περὶ τῆς αἰτήσεως τῆς μητρὸς τῶν υἱῶν Ζεβεδαίου. Προσελθοῦσα ἡ μήτηρ τῶν υἱῶν Ζεβεδαίου (οὓς Βοανεργὲς ἐκάλεσεν ὁ Σωτήρ) ᾐτεῖτο ἵνα εἷς ἐκ δεξιῶν καὶ εἷς ἐξ εὐωνύμων καθίσῃ ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ αὐτοῦ. Τοῖς μὲν μὴ δυναμένοις βάθη ζητεῖν ἀπλότης δοκεῖ ἡ αἴτησις· τοῖς δὲ βαθυτέροις καὶ ἡ ἀπόκρισις τοῦ Ἰησοῦ μέγα τι ἐμφαίνει. Ὥσπερ ἐπὶ κοσμικῆς βασιλείας τιμῶνται οἱ συγκαθεζόμενοι τῷ βασιλεῖ, οὕτως ὑπέλαβον καὶ οἱ δύο ἀπόστολοι ἔτι ἀτελεῖς ὄντες περὶ τῆς βασιλείας Χριστοῦ. Ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς φησίν· «Οὐκ οἴδατε τί αἰτεῖσθε» καὶ «Οὐκ ἔστιν ἐμὸν δοῦναι, ἀλλ’ οἷς ἡτοίμασται ὑπὸ τοῦ Πατρός μου.»
thought_title: The mother's request for seats in the kingdom
orientation: Origen is commenting on Matthew 20:20-23, where the mother of the sons of Zebedee asks Jesus that her sons sit at his right and left in his kingdom.
pass_a_gloss: Concerning the request of the mother of the sons of Zebedee. Having come forward the mother of the sons of Zebedee (whom Boanerges [he] called the Savior) was asking that one on [the] right and one on [the] left [he] might sit in the kingdom of him. To those indeed not being able depths to seek simplicity [it] seems the request; to those but deeper also the answer of Jesus [a] great thing indicates. Just as in [an] earthly kingdom [they] are honored the [ones] sitting with the king, so [they] supposed also the two apostles still incomplete being concerning the kingdom of Christ. The but Jesus says: "Not [you] know what [you] ask" and "Not [it] is mine to give, but [to those] for whom [it] has been prepared by the Father of me."

choices.why: Origen contrasts the surface reading with the deeper meaning; 'simplicity' preserves the Greek noun's sense of a naive, uncomplicated reading.
The comparative adjective refers to readers capable of seeking depths; 'those deeper' keeps the substantival use and the contrast with 'those not able to seek depths.'
The verb means to show forth or indicate; 'indicates something great' preserves the indefinite pronoun τι and the sense that the answer points to a hidden significance.
The participle with adverb marks their state at the time of the request; 'still being imperfect' keeps the temporal force and the theological sense of not yet mature.

choices.english: It is not mine to give
choices.why: The possessive adjective ἐμόν is emphatic; 'not mine to give' preserves the contrast with the Father's preparation.
rejected: I am not able to give
it is not for me to give

bible_refs.note: εἷς ἐκ δεξιῶν καὶ εἷς ἐξ εὐωνύμων καθίσῃ ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ αὐτοῦ
Οὐκ ἔστιν ἐμὸν δοῦναι, ἀλλ’ οἷς ἡτοίμασται ὑπὸ τοῦ Πατρός μου

pass_b_english: About the request of the mother of the sons of Zebedee. The mother of the sons of Zebedee—whom the Savior called Boanerges—came forward and was asking that one should sit at his right side and one at his left in his kingdom. To those who cannot seek depths, the request seems like simplicity; but to those deeper, Jesus' answer also indicates something great. Just as in a worldly kingdom those who sit with the king are honored, so the two apostles, still being imperfect, supposed about the kingdom of Christ. But Jesus says, "You do not know what you are asking" (Matthew 20:22), and "It is not mine to give, but it is for those for whom it has been prepared by my Father" (Matthew 20:23).

last_rejected.quote: The mother of the sons of Zebedee—whom the Savior called Boanerges—came forward
last_rejected.source_quote: Προσελθοῦσα ἡ μήτηρ τῶν υἱῶν Ζεβεδαίου (οὓς Βοανεργὲς ἐκάλεσεν ὁ Σωτήρ)
last_rejected.why: The Greek says the Savior called the sons Boanerges, not the mother; the dash makes it appear the mother was called Boanerges.
last_rejected.fix: The mother of the sons of Zebedee came forward—those whom the Savior called Boanerges—
last_rejected.ruling: οὓς is accusative masculine plural referring to the sons, not the mother; dash placement is ambiguous but not a clear mistranslation.

last_rejected.why: Imperfect indicates ongoing/repeated action, but 'was asking' obscures that she kept asking or persisted in the request.
last_rejected.ruling: 'Was asking' is a standard rendering of imperfect ᾐτεῖτο; no meaning is lost or changed.

last_rejected.why: 'Deeper' as substantive is awkward and unclear; Greek means 'to those who are deeper' or 'more profound persons', not 'to those deeper' as a comparative adjective standing alone.
last_rejected.ruling: 'To those deeper' is awkward but intelligible; τοῖς βαθυτέροις is within normal range, not a major error.

last_rejected.why: 'Supposed about' is not natural English; ὑπέλαβον means 'supposed/assumed' with an object, here that the kingdom of Christ was like worldly kingdoms.
last_rejected.fix: supposed the same of the kingdom of Christ
last_rejected.ruling: 'Supposed about' renders ὑπέλαβον περὶ adequately; awkwardness is not a major meaning change.

last_rejected.why: The citation Matthew 20:22 is wrong; this is Matthew 20:22 in modern numbering, but the verse reference should be checked: the first quote is Matt 20:22, second is Matt 20:23. last_rejected.ruling: Checker self-retracted; Matt 20:22 and 20:23 citations are correct.
